{{nihongo|'''Nyuu Shrine'''|丹生神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

=== Shrine crest ===
Circular mountain and water motif.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, around the time of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ar|الإمبراطور تيمو|arz|الامبراطور تيمو|azb|تمو|ca|Tenmu|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر تێنمو|cs|Temmu|de|Temmu|eo|Temmu|es|Tenmu Tennō|fa|امپراتور تنمو|fr|Tenmu|hak|Tenmu Thiên-fòng|he|טמו, קיסר יפן|hu|Tenmu japán császár|id|Kaisar Tenmu|it|Tenmu|ja|天武天皇|ka|ტენმუ|ko|덴무 천황|nl|Tenmu|pl|Tenmu|pt|Tenmu|ru|Император Тэмму|sh|Car Temmu|simple|Emperor Tenmu|sl|Cesar Tenmu|su|Kaisar Temmu|sv|Tenmu|th|จักรพรรดิเท็มมุ|tl|Emperador Temmu|tr|Temmu (imparator)|uk|Імператор Темму|vi|Thiên hoàng Tenmu|yo|Emperor Temmu|zh|天武天皇|zh_min_nan|Tenmu Thian-hông|zh_yue|天武天皇|qid=Q335181}}, Nyuu no Mahito enshrined the Nyuu deity on Mt. Tanbono. It is said to have been moved to the present site in {{ill|764|ab|764|af|764|am|764 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|764|ar|764|ary|764|ast|764|avk|764|az|764|azb|۷۶۴ (میلادی)|bar|764|be|764|be_x_old|764|bg|764|bn|৭৬৪|bpy|মারি ৭৬৪|br|764|bs|764.|ca|764|cdo|764 nièng|ceb|764|ckb|٧٦٤|crh|764|cs|764|cv|764|cy|764|da|764|de|764|el|764|eml|764|eo|764|es|764|et|764|eu|764|fa|۷۶۴ (میلادی)|fi|764|fo|764|fr|764|fy|764|ga|764|gan|764年|gd|764|gl|764|he|764|hi|764|hr|764.|ht|764 (almanak jilyen)|hu|764|hy|764|id|764|io|764|is|764|it|764|ja|764年|jv|764|ka|764|kk|764 жыл|ko|764년|la|764|lb|764|lij|764|lmo|764|lt|764 m.|map_bms|764|mdf|764|mg|764|mhr|764|mk|764|mr|इ.स. ७६४|mrj|764 и|ms|764|mzn|۷۶۴|nah|764|nap|764|nds|764|new|सन् ७६४|nl|764|nn|764|no|764|nrm|764|nso|764|oc|764|or|୭୬୪|os|764-æм аз|pl|764|pnb|764|pt|764|qu|764|ro|764|ru|764 год|rue|764|sa|७६४|scn|764|sd|764ع|sh|764.|shn|764|si|764|sk|764|sl|764|smn|764|sq|764|sr|764|su|764|sv|764|sw|764|tg|Соли 764|th|พ.ศ. 1307|tk|764|tl|764|tly|764|tr|764|tt|764 ел|uk|764|ur|764ء|uz|764|vec|764|vi|764|war|764|wuu|764年|xmf|764|zh|764年|zh_min_nan|764 nî|zh_yue|764年|qid=Q31163}} ({{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|de|Tempyō-Hōji|es|Tenpyō-hōji|fa|تنپیو-هوجی|fr|Ère Tenpyō-hōji|ia|Tenpyo-hoji|id|Tempyō-hōji|ja|天平宝字|ko|덴표호지|ru|Тэмпё-ходзи|simple|Tenpyō-hōji|sr|Тенпјо хоџи|tr|Tenpyō-hōji|uk|Темпьо-Ходзі (ненґо)|zh|天平宝字|zh_yue|天平寶字|qid=Q1346307}} 8). === Sacred grove ===
The surrounding area is designated as the "Nyuu Shrine Sacred Grove" under Shiga Prefecture's green environment conservation zones (area 1.78 ha; designated on August 30, 1989)<ref>{{Cite web|和書|date= |url=https://www.pref.shiga.lg.jp/file/attachment/21417.pdf |title=Shiga Environment 2009 |publisher=Shiga Prefecture |accessdate=2025-04-11}}</ref>.

It is enshrined in Yogo-cho Shimo-Nyuu. Like Kami-Nyuu, it is a disputed identification of an Engishiki shrine.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it was founded in {{ill|764|ab|764|af|764|am|764 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|764|ar|764|ary|764|ast|764|avk|764|az|764|azb|۷۶۴ (میلادی)|bar|764|be|764|be_x_old|764|bg|764|bn|৭৬৪|bpy|মারি ৭৬৪|br|764|bs|764.|ca|764|cdo|764 nièng|ceb|764|ckb|٧٦٤|crh|764|cs|764|cv|764|cy|764|da|764|de|764|el|764|eml|764|eo|764|es|764|et|764|eu|764|fa|۷۶۴ (میلادی)|fi|764|fo|764|fr|764|fy|764|ga|764|gan|764年|gd|764|gl|764|he|764|hi|764|hr|764.|ht|764 (almanak jilyen)|hu|764|hy|764|id|764|io|764|is|764|it|764|ja|764年|jv|764|ka|764|kk|764 жыл|ko|764년|la|764|lb|764|lij|764|lmo|764|lt|764 m.|map_bms|764|mdf|764|mg|764|mhr|764|mk|764|mr|इ.स. ७६४|mrj|764 и|ms|764|mzn|۷۶۴|nah|764|nap|764|nds|764|new|सन् ७६४|nl|764|nn|764|no|764|nrm|764|nso|764|oc|764|or|୭୬୪|os|764-æм аз|pl|764|pnb|764|pt|764|qu|764|ro|764|ru|764 год|rue|764|sa|७६४|scn|764|sd|764ع|sh|764.|shn|764|si|764|sk|764|sl|764|smn|764|sq|764|sr|764|su|764|sv|764|sw|764|tg|Соли 764|th|พ.ศ. 1307|tk|764|tl|764|tly|764|tr|764|tt|764 ел|uk|764|ur|764ء|uz|764|vec|764|vi|764|war|764|wuu|764年|xmf|764|zh|764年|zh_min_nan|764 nî|zh_yue|764年|qid=Q31163}} ({{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|de|Tempyō-Hōji|es|Tenpyō-hōji|fa|تنپیو-هوجی|fr|Ère Tenpyō-hōji|ia|Tenpyo-hoji|id|Tempyō-hōji|ja|天平宝字|ko|덴표호지|ru|Тэмпё-ходзи|simple|Tenpyō-hōji|sr|Тенпјо хоџи|tr|Tenpyō-hōji|uk|Темпьо-Ходзі (ненґо)|zh|天平宝字|zh_yue|天平寶字|qid=Q1346307}} 8). At the time of enshrinement it stood at the foot of Mt. Nyuho-Takayama, but it was moved to the present site in {{ill|870|Q23629|qid=Q23629}} ({{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} 12). The former site still has a small shrine known as Kagurano Myojin. The current shrine buildings are said to have been rebuilt in {{ill|1667|Q7588|qid=Q7588}} ({{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 7). It was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}} in {{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 9).
